content.text:
I've finished and submitted **index 0 (Nb 0.504 / V 0.496)** as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, **6.7 µA**. I don't know whether it's the best in the library, because 12 of the 15 compositions were never measured.

| Index | Nb fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | 0.72 (Nb-rich end) | 1.6 µA |
| 7 | 0.45 (V-rich end) | 5.5 µA |
| 0 | 0.50 (about 1:1) | 6.7 µA |

- **Order of measurements:** I measured both ends of the composition line first. The V-rich end was clearly better, so I spent the last measurement on the 1:1 Nb:V composition.
- **Why 1:1:** the model tools gave some support there. MACE puts NbVO5 nearly on the convex hull (0.027 eV/atom above it). MEGNet predicts a 1.8 eV band gap for one NbVO4 form, well below the 3.22 eV illumination, so it should absorb strongly.
- **Model limits:** MEGNet also predicts 3.5 eV for NbVO5, which is above the photon energy, so the band-gap predictions pointed both ways. I used them as weak guidance only.
- **What's left open:** the peak could lie nearer index 11 or 2, or at index 12, which the Gaussian-process model suggested. None of these were measured because all 3 merit measurements were used.
- **XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually present was never checked.
